papers.title: Gaussian Process Optimization with Adaptive Sketching: Scalable and No Regret
papers.abstract: Gaussian processes (GP) are a well studied Bayesian approach for the optimization of black-box functions. Despite their effectiveness in simple problems, GP-based algorithms hardly scale to high-dimensional functions, as their per-iteration time and space cost is at least quadratic in the number of dimensions $d$ and iterations $t$. Given a set of $A$ alternatives to choose from, the overall runtime $O(t^3A)$ is prohibitive. In this paper we introduce BKB (budgeted kernelized bandit), a new approximate GP algorithm for optimization under bandit feedback that achieves near-optimal regret (and hence near-optimal convergence rate) with near-constant per-iteration complexity and remarkably no assumption on the input space or covariance of the GP.   We combine a kernelized linear bandit algorithm (GP-UCB) with randomized matrix sketching based on leverage score sampling, and we prove that randomly sampling inducing points based on their posterior variance gives an accurate low-rank approximation of the GP, preserving variance estimates and confidence intervals. As a consequence, BKB does not suffer from variance starvation, an important problem faced by many previous sparse GP approximations. Moreover, we show that our procedure selects at most $\tilde{O}(d_{eff})$ points, where $d_{eff}$ is the effective dimension of the explored space, which is typically much smaller than both $d$ and $t$. This greatly reduces the dimensionality of the problem, thus leading to a $O(TAd_{eff}^2)$ runtime and $O(A d_{eff})$ space complexity.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文提出了一种可扩展的高斯过程优化方法，适用于高维黑箱函数优化，其自适应草图技术可迁移至生物力学代理模型中的高效采样与不确定性量化。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address FEA surrogate modeling, implant biomechanics, or any biomedical application; it focuses on theoretical GP optimization with no physical simulation validation.

summary_zh.motivation: 解决高维高斯过程优化中计算成本过高的问题

summary_en.motivation: To overcome the prohibitive computational cost of Gaussian process optimization in high-dimensional spaces.
summary_en.method: Combines GP-UCB with randomized matrix sketching via leverage score sampling to achieve near-constant per-iteration complexity.
summary_en.result: Achieves near-optimal regret with near-constant per-iteration complexity and avoids variance starvation.
summary_en.validation: Theoretical regret bounds and effective dimension analysis.
